id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

start.description: Start timestamp for the value.  If null, assumed to be beginning-of-time (BOT).

end.description: End timestamp for the value.  If null, assumed to be end-of-time (EOT).

from.description: The instance of {@link MlSubject} referenced by the relation.

to.description:
The {@link ReliabilityTteMlModel} referenced by the relation.

This field links the asset to a specific model from the `reliabilityTte` machine learning project.
The `ReliabilityTteMlModel` defines the time-to-event predictions and associated forecasts for the asset
and is crucial for tracking the performance and predictions of the model on the asset's life cycle.

The model could include various parameters such as failure probability, remaining useful life, and other
critical time-to-event metrics.

typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

route.description: The {@link MlModel.Route} that originated this relation.

status.description:
The deployment status of the relation, in particular if it is {@link MlModel.Route.Status.Label.CHAMPION CHAMPION},
{@link MlModel.Route.Status.Label.CHALLENGER CHALLENGER} or {@link MlModel.Route.Status.Label.RETIRED RETIRED}.

groupId.description:
The group ID of the relation, which is used to group together relations that were created as part of the same
batch. This can help optimize the fetch of these relations when doing batch operations.
For example, see {@link MlModel.Router#updateRouteBatch}.

timedPredictions.description:
A collection of time-based predictions related to the asset, including time-to-event predictions
generated by the model.
The `timedPredictions` field stores an array of predictions that are linked to specific time points.
These predictions may represent different types of time-to-event data, such as predicted failure times,
maintenance schedules, or other time-sensitive events related to the asset's performance.
The `parent` indicates that this field is sourced from the parent entity (which could be a time-series
or forecasting entity).

timedContributions.description:
A collection of time-based contributions associated with the asset, representing how different factors
or features contribute to the time-to-event predictions.
The `timedContributions` field stores an array of contributions at various time points, helping to understand
how different features (e.g., operating conditions, usage patterns) influence the predictions over time.
This is essential for model explainability and can help users identify which variables are most important
in forecasting the asset's time-to-event.
As with `timedPredictions`, this field is populated from the parent entity.

timedForecastPredictions.description:
A collection of time-based forecast predictions for the asset, representing forecasts of future time-to-event
outcomes based on the model.

`timedForecastPredictions` stores the forecasted predictions over a specific time horizon, such as predicted
failure times or maintenance schedules. These predictions provide an outlook into future events, based on the
model's understanding of the asset's behavior.

The field is useful for predictive maintenance, asset management, and planning future interventions.

timedForecastContributions.description:
A collection of time-based forecast contributions for the asset, showing how different factors contribute
to the forecasted time-to-event outcomes.

`timedForecastContributions` captures contributions for future time periods, offering insight into how
various factors will influence future forecasts. Understanding the factors contributing to the forecasted outcomes
can be useful for optimizing asset management strategies and improving the reliability of predictions.

reliabilityTimeToEventMLProjectId.description:
The id of the current reliability time-to-event {@link MlProject}. Fetched from {@link ReliabilityMLConfig}.

This field stores the ID of the time-to-event machine learning project, which provides a reference to the
model configuration and parameters used in the analysis. The ID is fetched from the `ReliabilityMLConfig`
configuration, ensuring that the asset is linked to the appropriate machine learning project.

This field allows the system to retrieve relevant configuration values and ensures that the correct models
are applied to the asset for analysis.

title:
An extension of {@link ReliabilityAssetToModelRelation} representing the relations between
a {@link ReliabilityAsset} and a model belonging to the `reliabilityTte` {@link MlProject}.
This entity type links an asset in the system (e.g., a machine or component) to a specific model within
the `reliabilityTte` machine learning project. It tracks the relationship between the asset and the model
along with various predictions, contributions, and forecast values related to time-to-event (TTE) modeling.
The relationship is essential for ensuring that the correct asset is associated with the appropriate model
and that the results of the TTE model (such as predictions and contributions) are linked to the asset in a
meaningful way for analysis and decision-making.
name: ReliabilityAssetToTteModelRelation
